authorProcess: Claude Code session (Research Intelligence PHASE 2, STEP 12) — design only, no computation

immutableInputs.rule: These records are not modified by STEP 12 or by any result of the follow-up study.

question: Can the V2 failure be attributed to reanalysis advection-field error in a low-energy (quiet-gyre) regime rather than to the absence of windage — i.e., does the same fixed model (alpha = 0.0007, no retuning) behave differently against the same baselines in a pre-defined advection-dominant cohort and with an independent current product?
notAQuestionAbout: making V1 or V2 PASS retrospectively; the 2015-01 quiet-gyre verdicts stand regardless of the answer

H1.statement: V2 windage is generally superior to V1.
H1.note: Already contradicted on the quiet-gyre cohort (C5 FAIL); the follow-up tests only whether this changes in a different regime.

H2.statement: In the 2015 North Atlantic quiet-gyre cohort the eddy/advection signal is weak, so the stationary baseline is intrinsically strong.
H2.testableBy: observed 72 h displacement distribution of the cohort versus the pre-registered advection-dominant threshold

H3.statement: In an advection-dominant regime the relative advantage of a current-driven model over the stationary baseline is larger.
H3.testableBy: C1-analog on the new cohort, same alpha, same metric

H4.statement: A different ocean reanalysis product (GLORYS12V1) yields different trajectory error than HYCOM GOFS 3.1 on the same cohort.
H4.testableBy: paired HYCOM-vs-GLORYS comparison on identical observations, horizons and metric

preregistrationRequirement: Before any follow-up computation: (1) cohort-selection-rule-v2.json applied and the chosen windows recorded, (2) validation-plan-v3.json with acceptance criteria committed alone, (3) GLORYS access obtained by the user (credentials are never entered by the assistant). None of these steps has been executed.
